text:
The correct statements from the following are :
$(A) Tl^{3+}$ is a powerful oxidising agent
$(B) Al^{3+}$ does not get reduced easily
(C) Both $Al^{3+}$ and $Tl^{3+}$ are very stable in solution
$(D) Tl^{1+}$ is more stable than $Tl^{3+}$
$(E) Al^{3+}$ and $Tl^{1+}$ are highly stable
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(i) True: $Tl^{1+}$ is more stable than $Tl^{3+}$ due to the inert pair effect. Therefore, $Tl^{3+}$ acts as a powerful oxidizing agent.

(ii) True: The standard reduction potential for $Al^{3+}/Al$ is -1.66 V, indicating that $Al^{3+}$ is difficult to reduce and thus highly stable.

(iii) False: $Tl^{3+}$ is not stable in solution.

(iv) True: $Tl^{1+}$ is more stable than $Tl^{3+}$.

(v) True: Both $Al^{3+}$ and $Tl^{1+}$ are highly stable in their respective oxidation states.

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : On hydrolysis, oligo peptides give rise to fewer number of α-amino acids while proteins give rise to a large number of β-amino acids.
Statement (II) : Natural proteins are denatured by acids which convert the water soluble form of fibrous proteins to their water insoluble form.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When oligopeptides undergo hydrolysis, they yield a small number of α-amino acids. In contrast, proteins do not produce β-amino acids upon hydrolysis. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Furthermore, natural proteins, when subjected to denaturation by acids, do not convert fibrous proteins from a water-soluble to a water-insoluble form, as fibrous proteins are inherently not water-soluble. Therefore, Statement II is also incorrect.

In conclusion, both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

text: A mixture of 1 g each of chlorobenzene, aniline, and benzoic acid is dissolved in 50 mL ethyl acetate and placed in a separating funnel. 5 M NaOH (30 mL) was added in the same funnel. The funnel was shaken vigorously and then kept aside. The ethyl acetate layer in the funnel contains :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Benzoic acid is a carboxylic acid, so aqueous NaOH converts it into sodium benzoate, an ionic salt that dissolves in the aqueous layer and leaves the ethyl acetate layer:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{NaOH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COONa}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Chlorobenzene (neutral; its aryl $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond is not attacked by aqueous NaOH under these conditions) and aniline (a base) do not react with NaOH, so both remain dissolved in ethyl acetate.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

solution.body:
The C–Cl bond of an aryl halide has partial double-bond character, so replacement of Cl by OH needs drastic conditions. A nitro group at the ortho or para position withdraws electrons by $-R$ and $-I$ effects and stabilises the negatively charged intermediate, so each additional o/p-nitro group lets the substitution proceed under milder conditions.

(A) Chlorobenzene has no activating group and needs NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification, to give phenol: (A)-(IV).

(B) 4-Nitrochlorobenzene, with one para nitro group, reacts with NaOH at 443 K: (B)-(III).

(C) 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene, with two nitro groups, reacts with NaOH at 368 K: (C)-(II).

(D) 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene, with three nitro groups, is hydrolysed by warm water alone to picric acid: (D)-(I).

The match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Liquid A and B form an ideal solution. The vapour pressures of pure liquids A and B are 350 and 750 mm Hg respectively at the same temperature. If $x_{A}$ and $x_{B}$ are the mole fraction of A and B in solution while $y_{A}$ and $y_{B}$ are the mole fraction of A and B in vapour phase, then,
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By Raoult's law $p_{A}=P_{A}^{\circ }x_{A}$ and $p_{B}=P_{B}^{\circ }x_{B}$, and by Dalton's law $y_{A}=p_{A}/P$ and $y_{B}=p_{B}/P$. Hence

$\dfrac{y_{A}}{y_{B}}=\dfrac{P_{A}^{\circ }}{P_{B}^{\circ }}\cdot \dfrac{x_{A}}{x_{B}}=\dfrac{350}{750}\cdot \dfrac{x_{A}}{x_{B}}=\dfrac{7}{15}\cdot \dfrac{x_{A}}{x_{B}}$

Since $\dfrac{7}{15}<1$, $\dfrac{y_{A}}{y_{B}}<\dfrac{x_{A}}{x_{B}}$, that is $\dfrac{x_{A}}{x_{B}}>\dfrac{y_{A}}{y_{B}}$: the vapour is richer in the more volatile liquid B. This rules out (B) and (C).

Because $x_{A}+x_{B}=1$ and $y_{A}+y_{B}=1$, $x_{B}-y_{B}=-(x_{A}-y_{A})$. A is less volatile, so $y_{A}<x_{A}$, giving $x_{A}-y_{A}>0>x_{B}-y_{B}$; (A) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift

text:
Match List - I with List - II.

  
    List - I
    List - II
  
  
    (A) Solution of chloroform and acetone
    (I) Minimum boiling azeotrope
  
  
    (B) Solution of ethanol and water
    (II) Dimerizes
  
  
    (C) Solution of benzene and toluene
    (III) Maximum boiling azeotrope
  
  
    (D) Solution of acetic acid in benzene
    $(IV) ΔV_{$mix} = 0
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To correctly match the items from List - I with those in List - II, let's analyze the characteristics of each solution:

(A) Solution of chloroform and acetone: This solution exhibits negative deviation from Raoult's law. It creates a maximum boiling azeotrope because the interactions between chloroform and acetone molecules are stronger than those in the pure components.

(B) Solution of ethanol and water: This solution shows positive deviation from Raoult's law, leading to the formation of a minimum boiling azeotrope. The interactions between ethanol and water molecules are weaker than those in their pure states.

(C) Solution of benzene and toluene: This combination forms an ideal solution where Raoult’s law is obeyed across all concentrations. Thus, the volume change upon mixing, denoted as $\Delta V_{\text{mix}}$, is zero.

(D) Solution of acetic acid in benzene: In this mixture, acetic acid tends to dimerize. The acetic acid molecules pair up, forming dimers, especially in non-polar solvents like benzene.

Based on these explanations, the correct matches are: 

(A) - (III)

(B) - (I)

(C) - (IV)

(D) - (II)

text:
The number of unpaired electrons responsible for the paramagnetic nature of the following complex species are respectively :
 [$Fe(CN)_{6}$]$^{3−}$, [FeF$_{6}$]$^{3−}$, [CoF$_{6}$]$^{3−}$, [$Mn(CN)_{6}$]$^{3−}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so the fluoro complexes are high spin; $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ is a strong-field ligand, so the cyano complexes are low spin, with electrons pairing in $t_{2g}$ before entering $e_{g}$.

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$; low spin $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$ leaves 1 unpaired electron.

$[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$; high spin $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ leaves 5 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$; high spin $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ has one doubly filled $t_{2g}$ orbital, leaving 4 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{4}$; low spin $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{0}$ leaves 2 unpaired electrons.

The numbers are 1, 5, 4, 2.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift

text:
A(g) → B(g) + C(g) is a first order reaction.

  
    
      Time
      t
      ∞
    
  
  
    
      $P_{$system}
      $P_{t}$
      $P_{$∞}
    
  

The reaction was started with reactant A only. Which of the following expressions is correct for rate constant k?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the initial pressure of A be $p^{\circ }$ and let it fall by $x$ in time $t$.


[IMG]

Total pressure at time $t$ and at completion:

$p_{t}=(p^{\circ }-x)+x+x=p^{\circ }+x,p_{\infty }=2p^{\circ }$

So $p^{\circ }=\dfrac{p_{\infty }}{2}$, $x=p_{t}-\dfrac{p_{\infty }}{2}$, and the pressure of A at time $t$ is

$p^{\circ }-x=\dfrac{p_{\infty }}{2}-p_{t}+\dfrac{p_{\infty }}{2}=p_{\infty }-p_{t}$

For a first order reaction, $k=\dfrac{1}{t}\ln \dfrac{p^{\circ }}{p^{\circ }-x}$:

$k=\dfrac{1}{t}\ln \dfrac{p_{\infty }/2}{p_{\infty }-p_{t}}=\dfrac{1}{t}\ln \dfrac{p_{\infty }}{2(p_{\infty }-p_{t})}$

Expression (D) takes $p_{\infty }$ as the initial pressure, but $p_{\infty }$ is twice the initial pressure because one molecule of gas gives two.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements :
 1 M aqueous solutions of each of $Cu(NO_{3})_{2}$, AgNO$_{3}, Hg_{2}(NO_{3})_{2}, Mg(NO_{3})_{2}$ are electrolysed using inert electrodes. Given: $E^{0}_{Ag^{+}/Ag} = 0.80 V, E^{0}_{Hg2}^{2+}/Hg = 0.79 V, E^{0}_{Cu^{2+}/Cu} = 0.24 V$ and $E^{0}_{Mg^{2+}/Mg} = -2.37 V$.
Statement (I) : With increasing voltage, the sequence of deposition of metals on the cathode will be Ag, Hg and Cu.
Statement (II) : Magnesium will not be deposited at the cathode instead oxygen gas will be evolved at the cathode.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let’s analyze the situation step by step.

We have 1 M aqueous solutions of:

$\text{AgNO}_{3}$ with $\text{Ag}^{+}/\text{Ag}E^{0}=+0.80V$

$\text{Hg}_{2}(\text{NO}_{3})_{2}$ with $\text{Hg}_{2}^{2+}/\text{Hg}E^{0}=+0.79V$

$\text{Cu(NO}_{3})_{2}$ with $\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}E^{0}=+0.24V$

$\text{Mg(NO}_{3})_{2}$ with $\text{Mg}^{2+}/\text{Mg}E^{0}=-2.37V$

In an electrolytic cell with inert electrodes, reduction occurs at the cathode. The ion with the highest (most positive) reduction potential will be reduced (or deposited) first. Therefore, as we increase the applied voltage (making the cathode sufficiently negative), the metals will begin to deposit in the order of their reduction potentials.

The order of reduction (deposition) will be:

First, silver ($+0.80V$)

Next, mercury ($+0.79V$)

Then, copper ($+0.24V$)

So, Statement (I) which says “With increasing voltage, the sequence of deposition of metals on the cathode will be Ag, Hg and Cu” is correct.

For magnesium, the reduction potential is very negative ($-2.37V$). In aqueous solution, before reaching such a negative potential, water will be reduced. The cathodic reaction for water typically is:

$2~\text{H}_{2}\text{O}+2e^{-}\to \text{H}_{2}+2\text{OH}^{-}$

which leads to the evolution of hydrogen gas, not oxygen. (Oxygen is produced at the anode during the oxidation of water.)

Hence, Statement (II) erroneously states that “oxygen gas will be evolved at the cathode” when in fact, if magnesium were to be reduced (which it won’t be), water reduction would yield hydrogen gas. Thus, Statement (II) is incorrect.

Summary:

Statement (I) is correct.

Statement (II) is incorrect.

Therefore, the most appropriate answer is:

Option C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift

text:
The extra stability of half-filled subshell is due to :

(A) Symmetrical distribution of electrons

(B) Smaller coulombic repulsion energy

(C) The presence of electrons with the same spin in non-degenerate orbitals

(D) Larger exchange energy

(E) Relatively smaller shielding of electrons by one another 

Identify the correct statements :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A half-filled subshell ($p^{3}$, $d^{5}$, $f^{7}$) has one electron in each degenerate orbital, all with parallel spins; this symmetrical distribution of electrons gives extra stability, so (A) is correct.

With one electron per orbital, no two electrons are paired in the same orbital, so the coulombic repulsion energy is smaller; (B) is correct.

Electrons with parallel spins in degenerate orbitals can exchange their positions, and the number of such exchanges is maximum in a half-filled subshell, so the exchange energy released is larger; (D) is correct.

Electrons of the same subshell shield one another relatively poorly, so each experiences a higher effective nuclear charge; (E) is correct.

Exchange stabilisation arises from parallel-spin electrons in degenerate orbitals (equal-energy orbitals of one subshell), not in non-degenerate orbitals, so (C) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift

text:
'X' is the number of acidic oxides among $VO_{2}, V_{2}O_{3}$, CrO$_{3}, V_{2}O_{5}$ and $Mn_{2}O_{7}$. The primary valency of cobalt in 
[$Co(H_{2}$NCH$_{2}CH_{2}NH_{2})_{3}$]$_{2}(SO_{4})_{3}$ is Y. The value of X + Y is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acidic character of a metal oxide rises with the oxidation state of the metal.

$\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$ (V +3) is basic. $\mathrm{VO}{}_{2}$ (V +4) dissolves in acids to give $\mathrm{VO}{}^{2+}$ salts and in alkalis to give vanadates(IV), so it is amphoteric. $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ (V +5) is amphoteric, though mainly acidic, since it gives both $\mathrm{VO}{}_{4}{}^{3-}$ and $\mathrm{VO}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ salts.

$\mathrm{CrO}{}_{3}$ (Cr +6) and $\mathrm{Mn}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$ (Mn +7) are acidic oxides: with water they give $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}{}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{HMnO}{}_{4}$. Hence $X=2$.

The complex ionises as

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{NCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}){}_{3}]{}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}){}_{3}\longrightarrow 2[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{3}]{}^{3+}+3\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$

The primary valency of the metal is its oxidation state, satisfied by the ionisable counter-ions. Ethane-1,2-diamine (en) is neutral, so cobalt is +3 and $Y=3$.

$X+Y=2+3=5$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The standard state of a substance at a specified temperature is its pure form at 1 bar; no particular temperature is part of the definition (data are usually tabulated at 298 K only by choice). So statements (A) and (D) are incorrect.

The standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its reference (most stable) form is zero at every temperature, since forming the element from itself involves no change. $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ is the reference form of oxygen, so $\Delta _{f}H_{500}^{\circ }$ of $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ is zero, and (B) is correct.

Atomic oxygen is not the reference form: $\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$ requires breaking the O=O bond, so $\Delta _{f}H_{298}^{\circ }$ of $\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$ is about $+249\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, not zero. So (C) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
In Dumas' method 292 mg of an organic compound released 50 mL of nitrogen gas $(\mathrm{N}_{2})$ at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of ' N ' in the organic compound is $_____________$ % (Nearest integer)
(Aqueous tension at $300\mathrm{K}=15\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given:

Volume of $N_{2}$, $V=50$ mL

Pressure, $P=715$ mm Hg

Temperature, $T=300$ K

Aqueous Tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg

Calculation:

Correct the Pressure for $N_{2}$:

$P_{N_{2}}=715\text{mmHg}-15\text{mmHg}=700\text{mmHg}$

Convert the pressure from mm Hg to atm:

$P_{N_{2}}=\frac{700}{760}\text{atm}$

Calculate the Moles of $N_{2}$ using the Ideal Gas Law:

$n_{N_{2}}=\frac{P_{N2}\cdot V}{R\cdot T}$

$n_{N_{2}}=\frac{\frac{700}{760}\times \frac{50}{1000}}{0.0821\times 300}$

Calculate the Moles of $N$:

$n_{N}=2\times n_{N_{2}}$

Calculate the Mass of $N$:

$\text{Mass of}N=2\times n_{N}\times 14$

Determine the Percentage of Nitrogen in the Organic Compound:

$%N=\frac{\text{Mass of}N}{\text{Mass of organic compound}}\times 100$

$%N=\frac{\frac{700}{760}\times \frac{50}{1000}\times 2\times 14}{0.0821\times 300}\times \frac{1000}{292}\times 100$

$%N=18%$

The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is 18%.

text:
Butane reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water following the equation given below.

$\mathrm{C}_{4}\mathrm{H}_{10}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{13}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to 4\mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+5\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$

If 174.0 kg of butane is mixed with 320.0 kg of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$, the volume of water formed in liters is

$_____________. ($Nearest integer)

[Given : (a) Molar mass of C, H, O are $12,1,16\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively, (b) Density of water $\left. =1\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mL}^{-1}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Moles taken: $n(\mathrm{C}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{10})=\dfrac{174.0\times 10^{3}}{58}=3000$ mol and $n(\mathrm{O}{}_{2})=\dfrac{320.0\times 10^{3}}{32}=10000$ mol.

$3000$ mol of butane needs $3000\times \dfrac{13}{2}=19500$ mol of $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$, but only $10000$ mol is present, so $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ is the limiting reagent and butane is in excess.

$\dfrac{13}{2}$ mol of $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ gives $5$ mol of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$:

$n(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O})=10000\times \dfrac{5}{13/2}=\dfrac{10^{5}}{13}=7692.3\text{mol}$

Mass of water $=7692.3\times 18=1.3846\times 10^{5}$ g $=138.46$ kg.

Density $1\text{g mL}^{-1}=1\text{kg L}^{-1}$, so the volume of water $=138.46$ L $\approx 138$ L.

Hence, the answer is 138.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift

text: The number of paramagnetic metal complex species among $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+},[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4})_{3}]^{3-}$, $[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{FeF}_{6}]^{3-}$ with same number of unpaired electrons is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The metal ions are $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$) in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$, $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$; $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{4}$) in $[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$; and $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{5}$) in $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$.

For the highly charged $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ion, $\Delta _{o}$ exceeds the pairing energy with all common ligands other than $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$. So $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$ and $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$ are low spin, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, with 0 unpaired electrons (diamagnetic), while $[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ is high spin, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, with 4 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ (weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$) is $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$ with 4 unpaired electrons, and $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ (strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$) is $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{0}$ with 2.

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ is $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$ with 1 unpaired electron, and $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ is $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ with 5.

The five paramagnetic species have 4, 2, 4, 1 and 5 unpaired electrons, so only $[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ have the same number (4).

Hence, the answer is 2.

text:
One litre buffer solution was prepared by adding 0.10 mol each of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$ in deionised water. The change in pH on addition of 0.05 mol of HCl to the above solution is $______________$ $\times 10^{-2}$.

(Nearest integer)

Given : $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}$ of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}=4.745$ and $\log _{10}3=0.477$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The buffer holds $0.10$ mol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and $0.10$ mol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$ in 1 L, so

$\mathrm{pOH}=\mathrm{p}K_{b}+\log \dfrac{[\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}]}{[\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}]}=4.745+\log 1=4.745$

The added HCl converts an equal amount of base into its conjugate acid, $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}\qquad +\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$, leaving $0.10-0.05=0.05$ mol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and $0.10+0.05=0.15$ mol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$.

$\mathrm{pOH}^{'}=4.745+\log \dfrac{0.15}{0.05}=4.745+\log 3=4.745+0.477=5.222$

The pOH rises by 0.477, so the pH falls by the same amount, from $14-4.745=9.255$ to $14-5.222=8.778$:

$|\Delta \mathrm{pH}|=0.477=47.7\times 10^{-2}\approx 48\times 10^{-2}$

Hence, the answer is 48.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Evening Shift
